document_metadata.document_title: Urban Storm Drainage Criteria Manual Volume 3 (MHFD/UDFCD) — regional Front Range reference

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Water Quality Capture Volume (WQCV) based on runoff from 0.6 inches of precipitation within the MHFD/UDFCD boundary (≈80th percentile storm); remaining runoff after volume reduction treated through capture and slow release of the WQCV. City drainage portals often HTML/403 — Front Range MS4s commonly apply USDCM Volume 3.

evidence.excerpt: City of Colorado Springs Front Range MS4 — coverage via MHFD/UDFCD Volume 3 WQCV
Water Quality Capture Volume (WQCV) based on runoff from 0.6 inches
Within the UDFCD boundary, the WQCV is based on runoff from 0.6 inches of precipitation.
evidence.page_or_section: Chapter 1, Common Stormwater Management Terms, page 11

evidence.excerpt: Bioretention (rain gardens): The use of distributed on-site vegetated features such as rain gardens can help maintain natural drainage patterns
permeable pavement systems, bioretention, extended detention basins, sand filters, constructed wetland ponds, and retention ponds

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Corpus is USDCM Vol. 3 Chapter 1 (planning/regulatory). WQCV defined as runoff from 0.6 in. precipitation within UDFCD boundary (~80th percentile storm). Step 2 BMPs named; detailed sizing/dimensions referenced in Chapters 3–5, not in these excerpts.
